newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end higher on President Lee promise.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end higher on President Lee promise.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed fairly higher on Monday after President Lee Teng-hui promised on Saturday that the government would solve businesses' land obtaining problem within six months, brokers said.
The weighted index ended up 53.91 points or 0.83 percent at 6,518.46. Turnover was a modest T$39.14 billion.
Domestic demand-oriented shares such as financials, cements and foods rose on Lee's promise.
"Domestic demand-oriented shares took turns to rise, triggering the overall upward momentum to break resistance at 6,500 points," said Michael Hung of Nikko Securities.
Buying in electronics emerged also after the Wall Street market hit a new record high, brokers said.

"Electronics rose (0.99 percent) to react to Wall Street's hitting new high led by high-tech shares," Hung said. "But Taiwan's electronics, due to being the upstream of the U.S. high-tech firm industry, has already risen one month earlier."
Financials led the gains, with Chinatrust up 50 cents to T$53. Some textiles rose on polyester fibre price hikes, with Shinkong Synthetic Fibre up 20 cents to T$24.5.
Brokers noted continuous bullish sentiment boosted by rising foreign fund inflows since August.
"Monday's rise was also a typical liquidity-driven gain triggered by rising foreign fund inflows and loose liquidity in the local money market," Hung said.
Brokers said they expected a firming trend in coming sessions.
"Some local industries have gradually shown improving fundamentals, likely to back up a firming trend for the index to test 6,600 points in coming sessions," Hung said.
A 6,500-6,550 range was seen for Tuesday.
